ety.text: From Pitman ess and eff, which it resembles phonetically and graphically, and the sound it represents. The change in vowel probably reflects the familiar suffix -ish.
Phonetic spelling of the clipping of issue.
From earlier isht, a minced oath and metathetic alteration of shit. Possibly onomatopoeic from being inspired by the sound of the word shit when backmasked in clean or radio edits of hip-hop songs.

ex: The exam went well... mostly... ish.
'With luck, about twelve.' 'Ah,' said Bernard. 'Twelve-thirty. Ish.'
How old are you? Fifty-ish?" / "Ish." / The color flared in her cheeks but she didn't look as though she were going to shoot me.

senses.d: The letter which stands for the sh sound /ʃ/ in Pitman shorthand.
An instalment of a periodical; an issue.
ex: Next ish: a guide to who is who of the Howard heroes in the centerspread.
My sincerest apologies to Brother Ron Smith in the December ish.
Anyone, really, but seriously, you'd think that people whose very passion depends on their lungs would want to cut that ish out
I owe you a lot Dipal, so put that ish away.

fr:à peu près.gl: more or less; about, just about
